en:
Designed to meet Japan's "kei car" standards, the Copen
is a 2-seat convertible with an FF layout.

While it may only sport a 660cc engine, you'd do well to
not underestimate it!

A perfect car for those who like a bit of power, the Copen
also boasts a rigid chassis and precise handling.

Its electrically operated metal roof is also quite the
crowd-pleaser!

The first generation Dodge Viper made a splash in the
sports car world when it made its debut.

It was a stylish FR sports car with a potent V-10 engine.

Some were so awed by its prowess that they began calling it
the Corvette killer.

Did you know that Lamborghini was involved in developing
the Viper's engine and suspension?

That's because back then, Dodge and Lamborghini
were both owned by Chrysler.

Released in 1996, the Viper GTS had even more torque and
power than the original.

This second-generation Viper was released in 2002.

Its 8.4-liter V-10 possessed 400cc more displacement
than the previous model.

This translated to more than 600ps of power!

What's more, it weighed 50kg less than
its predecessor!

It was developed and bred on the Nürburgring test track
in Germany.

This model was a force on many race circuits
around the world.

BMW obtained the rights and resurrected the popular
British car known as the Mini in 2001.

The folks at BMW were careful to keep the car's signature
compact boxy design intact.

This particular model is the high-performance Cooper S.

It boasts a peppy supercharged 1.6-liter inline-4 engine.

Thanks to its rigid chassis and solid structure, this car
has the feel of a go-kart when you push it to it limits.

If you're looking for a mid-engine V-8 Ferrari, you can't go
wrong with the F430.

This successor to the 360 Modena boasts an additional 90ps
of power...

...coming from a sweet-sounding engine.

The F430 came with carbon ceramic brakes and a
computer-controlled LSD called the E-Diff.

To this day, few production cars can match the F430's
performance on the circuit!

The Spirit R was the last rendition of the third-generation
RX-7, and it may just be the best of the lot.

Three versions of the Spirit R were produced, including
the Type A that you see here.

All third-gen RX-7s, dubbed the FD, were 2-seaters.

The Spirit R also came with enhanced suspension and braking
that made it really shine on the race track.

This beauty is a modern remake of the legendary Ford GT40.

Some say that it's one of Ford's greatest masterpieces!

You can really tell that its design was inspired by
the beautiful race cars of the 1960s.

As it happens, this model was made to celebrate Ford's
100th anniversary.

It's a true classic!

If you're a fan of racing, then you should be familiar with
the Audi R8, which dominated Le Mans in the early 2000s?

Well, that's where this particular version gets its name!

This first-generation R8 is an absolute must-buy
for supercar lovers.

It's a mid-engine car with a 4.2-liter V-8
that pumps out 420ps.

In addition to employing Audi's quattro
all-wheel drive technology...

...it was noted for its uniquely lightweight aluminum
body structure called the Audi Space Frame.

This tuned Honda S2000 was produced by Powerhouse Amuse,
some of the best Honda tuners in the business!

They turbo-charged the S2000's 2L F20C straight-four engine
and enlarged it to 2.3L—producing 626ps of power!

The body kit was developed in collaboration with the
developers of Gran Turismo.

Its longer nose and added diffuser make this model as
aerodynamic as any fully-fledged racing car.

You won't know how smooth a ride can be until you take
one of these for a spin!

RE Amemiya is a legendary Japanese tuner of Mazda cars.

Specializing in enhancing rotary engines, it has produced
a number of high-powered RX-7 over the years.

The RE Amemiya FD3S RX-7, also known as the Amemiya µ
Boost up 7, is one of the company's most iconic models.

Its power and flawless balance make it an absolute
monster on the race track.

You'll be amazed to see how well it takes corners!

The V-Spec II Nür was the last version of the
Skyline GT-R (R34) that Nissan produced.

It featured an improved L6 twin-turbo RB26DETT engine
that delivered better responsiveness and torque.

This ultra-rare model had an extremely limited
production run.

This means that it's already a collector's item,
so be sure to put one in your Garage.

This fifth-generation Nissan Fairlady Z was codenamed Z33.
We know it better as the 350Z.

The Z was temporarily discontinued in 2000 with the 300ZX,
codenamed Z32.

It was revived in 2002 with the 350Z.

This specific model is from 2007, and it features massive
improvements to its naturally-aspirated V-6 powerplant.

In fact, this little beauty is capable of more than 300ps
with added torque to make it quick off the line.

The highlight of this fourth-generation BMW M3
was its naturally-aspirated V-8 engine.

It was the first engine of its kind in an M3. With an 8400rpm
redline, it packed a potent high-end punch.

If you want to know what a race car for the street feels like,
then be sure to take a drive in this thing.

This improved Honda NSX Type R, also known as the 02R,
was released in 2002.

Its lightweight body and sport-tuned suspension made it
a monster on the track.

Part of the reason was an excellent aerodynamic shape
that allowed the car to generate gobs of downforce.

You'll be hard-pressed to find a car that feels as good to
drive as this one.

This is Suzuki's Swift Sport, an iconic Japanese FF hot hatch.

It served as a great foundation for a rally race car. Just look
at its performances at the Junior World Rally Championship.

Okay, so maybe the 1.6-liter naturally-aspirated engine sounds
unimpressive at first...

...but this thing featured variable valve-timing technology,
and forged pistons!

It came mated to a close-ratio 5-speed manual, making the car
a hoot to drive on the race track.

sourceName: Ford GT LM Spec II Test Car
en:
This Gran Turismo-exclusive Gr.3 race car is based on
the Ford GT.

Conceived as a "Ford GT for Le Mans,"...

...the car came with a specially designed suspension system
and a race-ready 6-speed manual transmission.

All of its body panels were constructed from carbon fiber
to reduce weight as much as possible.

Therefore, it tips the scales at only 1150kg!

Nissan's S15 Silvia has become one of the most popular
Japanese rear-wheel-drive sports cars, thanks to drifting.

This particular version is the Spec-R Aero that came with the
SR20 turbocharged inline-4 engine.

The car has classic sports-car proportions
and weighs only 1200kg.

If you enjoy sliding your car around corners, then you'll be
delighted with the balance that this thing delivers.%

This sixth-generation 2009 370Z was known in-house as the Z34.

It came with a redesigned naturally-aspirated 3.7-liter V-6.

This engine produced 336ps, which represented a significant
bump from the 3.5-liter unit of its predecessor.

It came mated to a 6-speed manual gearbox
with a new rev-matching technology.

Called SynchroRev, it automatically matched engine speed
to wheel speed during downshifts.

This allowed the driver to perform perfect downshifts without
having to employ a technique called heel-and-toe.

The 2008 Nissan Xanavi Nismo GT-R certainly made its
mark on racing history.

This car gave Nissan the Super GT championship in 2008.

Powered by a 4.5-liter V-8 engine based on the VK45DE.

And, unlike the 4-wheel-drive GT-R, the racing model employed
an FR layout, which is front-engine, rear-wheel drive.

Some called the V8 Vantage the "baby Aston."

The car was lower priced than the company's flagship
and had a smaller engine.

But the car still possessed plenty of performance,
more than most cars on the market at the time.

This Vantage S was a high-performance version that put out
10ps more than the base car.

It also came with an enhanced suspension system
and quicker steering.

This is Alfa Romeo's supercar, the 8C Competizione.

It sports a mighty V-8 engine that was built
at a Ferrari factory.

Not only is it powerful, it also sounds sweet.

This car has an FR layout with a rear-mounted transaxle.

You'll find it handles like a dream, thanks to its excellent
weight balance.

It's beautiful appearance was inspired by classic
racing Alfa Romeos from the 1930s and 1940s.

The appearance of this FF hot hatch bears a strong resemblance
to the Alfa Romeo 8C.

The power of its turbocharged 1.4-liter inline-4 engine makes
its presence known when you stomp the throttle pedal.

It's a fantastic car with an excellent suspension system.

The car stays glued to the pavement on high-speed corners!|

This formidable machine may be one of the most exquisite
road cars Aston Martin has ever produced.

Called the One-77, it remains one of the company's
most exclusive models.

It possesses a full carbon-fiber monocoque chassis.

It also has a pushrod suspension system,
usually reserved for race cars.

Under the hood is a naturally-aspirated V-12 engine
that pumps out 760ps!

As its name suggests, production of the car was limited to
77 units, making it a highly sought collector's item.i

Carving through a corner with absolute precision
captures the very essence of driving.

Few automakers have pursued that sensation with as
much single-minded determination as Caterham.

Introduced in 1999, the Superlight R500 represented
the most extreme expression of the iconic Seven.

With extensive use of lightweight materials, the R500
tipped the scales at a mere 500kg.

In 2008, it was refitted with a 2-liter Ford Duratec engine
producing 266ps and ample torque in the low-to-mid rpm range.

The R500 name reflected its remarkable
500-horsepower-per-ton power-to-weight ratio.

Free of electronic driver aids and unnecessary comforts, it
remains a vivid reminder of what a pure sports car can be.

This ZR1 is the most potent version of the sixth-generation
Corvette.

It came with a hand-built and supercharged
V-8 engine that...

...pumped out an impressive 647ps and 80kgm of torque.

This is one flexible engine, with gobs of power coming
throughout the rpm spectrum.

It made waves when it first appeared by beating the
Nissan GT-R's time on the Nürburgring Nordschleife.

And what's really cool about this American sports car
is that it handles as good as it goes straight.

This Enzo is a special car that celebrated the company's
55th anniversary.

Released in 2002 as a successor to the F40 and F50...

...the Enzo was a mid-engine car with a naturally-aspirated
6.0-liter V-12 that produced 660ps.

Designed by Ken Okuyama, who worked for
Pininfarina at the time...

...the Enzo's front end was modelled after a Formula 1 car.

And if you're wondering about its name,
Enzo Ferrari was the name of the company's founder.

This third-generation FIAT 500 was the quintessential
Italian compact car.

Not only did it inherit its design from the popular
second-generation model...

...but like its predecessor, it was a tremendous success,
selling in huge numbers all over the world.

With a free-revving 1.2-liter 70ps engine...

...its nimble handling made it a joy to drive!

The Italian powerhouse Abarth has long been a
revered name in motorsport...

...but also for its expertise in tuning FIATs.

This symbol of Abarth's revival in 2007... combined a 135ps
turbo engine with the compact lightweight body of a FIAT 500.

You would be wrong to underestimate this car
because it behaves like a real sports car!

Succeeding the awesome Lamborghini Diablo was the Murciélago,
equipped with a V-12 engine.

The LP 640 is a high-performance version that was unveiled in
2006 with 4-wheel drive and a 640ps engine.

And, did you know that the basic structure of the engine is
identical to that of the legendary Countach?

In fact, the Murciélago was the last Lamborghini model
to use this engine.

It definitely belongs with the likes of the Countach
and Diablo.

Maserati has always produced amazing sports coupes...

And this GranTurismo S was no exception, following in
the company's great tradition.

Not only was its engine one of the most powerful offered
by the Italian car maker...

...it also came with a transaxle, where the transmission
and rear axle are combined.

With both style and substance, GranTurismo S is definitely
the enthusiast's touring car.

The partnership between Mercedes-Benz and McLaren was one of
the most successful in the history of Formula 1.

This SLR McLaren was a product of that historic
collaboration.

Its design was inspired by Mercedes-Benz's legendary
300 SLR race car.

It featured a carbon fiber monocoque body
and came powered by a supercharged V-8.

And was this engine ever powerful? It pumped out more than
600ps and 80kgm of torque!

The Super GT is Asia's most prestigious GT race series,
and one of the stars of the show is the NSX.

This particular model is the EPSON NSX, which raced
under the Nakajima Racing banner in 2008.

Although production of the NSX temporarily stopped in 2002...

...Honda continued to race it in the Super GT, while continuing
development of the car.

This EPSON car was the only NSX at the time
to run on Dunlop tires.

This meant that it wasn't able to share data with other Honda
teams, but that didn't stop it from dominating on the track!

When it comes to super expensive, super exotic machines,
Pagani has few equals. Take for example the Zonda R.

Its raw performance suggests that it was designed for
track use, and it was.

Thanks partly to its carbon-fiber body, it
weighs only 1250kg.

Under its hood is a V-12 engine based on the one in the
Mercedes-Benz CLK-GTR.

This combination was lethal, as it lapped the Nürburgring
Nordschleife in an impressive 6:47.50 in 2010.

And yeah, that was a new world record at the time.

When it comes to collectable Porsches, the Carrera GT
is definitely high on everyone's list.

It came equipped with a naturally-aspirated V-10 powerplant
mounted amidships...

...mated to a 6-speed manual gearbox.

It looked the part, too, with an attractive body style that
gave Ferraris a run for their money.

If you're a Porsche fan, then this car belongs in your garage.S

This race car was developed for the Renault Eurocup Mégane
Trophy, a one-make racing series held by Renault Sport.

Now it may share its name with the Renault Mégane, but
this is no family car—it was built for the circuit!

Powered by a mid-mounted 3.5-liter V-6,
and sporting a steel-frame body.

Its low weight provides excellent handling
balance, making it a beast on the race track.

The Prius was the world's first mass-produced hybrid car.
This is the third generation model, released in 2009.

The hybrid system in the third-gen model, introduced in 2009,
was 90% revamped, highlighted by a 1.8-liter inline-4.

The chassis was also significantly improved, making it a
smooth performer on the highway.

Oh, its fuel economy was enhanced as well, which meant that it
remained one of the most fuel-efficient cars in the world.S

Among the more noteworthy things about the BMW Z8 was that
it served as James Bond's main ride for a few movies.

While many said it was a sin that Agent 007 had a German car,
you can't argue with its beautiful 507-inspired design.

Under its hood was a 5.0-liter V-8 engine that produced
an impressive 400ps and 51kgm.

It was a true driver's car, thanks to its 6-speed
manual gearbox.

What you're looking at is the spiritual successor
to the legendary 300 SL.

The car's long nose and very fancy gullwing doors were
inspired by those of its predecessor.

The SLS AMG came powered by a 6.3-liter V-8
that produced a whopping 571ps.

While AMG is generally known for creating high-performance
versions of production Mercedes-Benz models...

...this baby was designed completely from scratch.

If you're looking for a mid-engine Ferrari with a naturally-
aspirated V-8, then look no further than the 458 Italia.

Its high-powered engine is capable of revving to 9000rpm.

And if you mash the throttle pedal and let it scream,
you'll unleash 570ps of power!

And the 7-speed dual-clutch gearbox allows you to shift
like a Formula 1 race driver.

Lexus has been competing in the GT500 class of the
Super GT series since 2006.

Its first car was the SC 430, which did battle in the
GT500 class.

The car took over the hugely successful Toyota A80 Supra
as Toyota's main entry in the series.

This model, the PETRONAS TOM'S SC 430, captured the
team title for TOM'S in 2008.

The GT by Citroën, unveiled in 2008, was a collaboration
between Citroën and Gran Turismo.

The car you see here is the road-going version of
the concept.

While the original study was powered by electricity, this one
came equipped with a mid-mounted gasoline V-8.

The body was penned by Takumi Yamamoto, a designer
at Citroën.

The lines of the car suggest the intricacies
of Japanese samurai armor.D

The 908 HDi FAP is the peak of Peugeot's racing
history at Le Mans.

Designed to compete in the 24-hour race, the French
company pulled no punches in its development.

It wasn't until 2009 that it finally bested the mighty
Audi R10 to win the overall title.

The car you see here is the 2010 model.

It didn't win Le Mans, but it did grab the top four
spots in qualifying, an incredible feat in itself!

McLaren has made more than a few noteworthy road cars...

...and among them is the MP4-12C, the first one since
the legendary F1.

Its single-piece carbon-fiber monocoque was the first of
its kind in a production car.

The car's active suspension system was also an
engineering marvel.

Powering this beauty was a twin-turbocharged 3.8-liter V-8,
mounted amidships and pumping out 600ps!

We had to wait a long time to get a successor to the F1,
but the MP4-12C made it all worth it.

Even after several generations, the original Audi TT
still manages to look and feel fresh.

It shared its chassis with the Audi A3, although the
wheelbase was shortened by 90mm.

Its compact nature made it incredibly agile.

Here is the 3.2 quattro, which was added to the lineup
in 2003.

Its smooth 3.2-liter V-6 engine sent 250ps to
all four wheels.

This version of the SLS AMG was developed to comply
with FIA GT3 regulations.

While the engine was unchanged from the production model
its sequential 6-speed transmission was built for racing.

The car was also much more aerodynamic than its predecessor.

It made its debut in 2011, where it entered 101 races
and won 25 of them.

If you're searching for a powerful FF sports car,
I would recommend the Scirocco R.

It comes with upgraded suspension and brakes, and turbocharged
2.0-liter inline-4 that produced 250ps.

While its specs are similar to the Golf R, it is about 120kg
lighter, thanks to the absence of the 4WD system.

You can really feel the weight difference when
taking sharp corners.B

Flashy scissor doors and big V-12 engines have been signatures
of Lamborghini for a while now.

Every flagship model produced by the company since
the Countach had them.

As did the 2011 Aventador.

The engine in this beauty pumped out a massive 700ps.

The car also featured a carbon-fiber monocoque and a pushrod
suspension system.

Needless to say, it was designed for the race track although
it was an easy car to drive on the open road.

The BMW Z4 GT3 is a FIA GT3 race car.

This 2011 model came with a 4.4-liter V-8 engine
that delivered 515ps.

The gear changes were made through a sequential 6-speed
manual transmission with paddle shifters.

Not only did the car score two wins in the FIA GT3
European Championship...

...it also shone at the Nürburgring and Spa
24- hour endurance races.

At both venues, it claimed an impressive second place!

This tuned Mazda MX-5 was based on the
first-generation model.

Nearly every aspect of the car was improved, from its engine
to its upgraded suspension system.

It was also lightened and made more durable.

The changes to its chassis resulted in a more neutral handling
balance, which makes it a blast to drive on the race track.M

Austrian manufacturer KTM is generally known for
producing high-performance motorcycles.

But it changed the script with the X-Bow.

This mid-engine car comes equipped with turbocharged
2.0-liter engine built by Audi.

Despite being an automobile, the X-Bow still has the feel
of a motorcycle, with no doors or windows.

What's more, its carbon-fiber monocoque structure makes it
incredibly lightweight at 790kg.

As the name suggests, the M3 GT is a race car based on
the venerable M3.

It was developed for the FIA GT2 category, which allows cars
to be significantly modified.

Under its hood was a tuned V-8 that pumped out 500ps,
which represents a slight increase from the base car.

It also weighed a lot less than the road car, thanks to
the copious use of carbon-fiber in the body panels.

The combination proved successful as it took the overall title
at the Nürburgring 24 Hours in 2010.

You're looking at the Audi's prototype race car called
the R18 TDI.

Built in 2011, the R18 TDI was primarily used in endurance
races such as the 24 Hours of Le Mans.

It was raced by Team Joest, which worked closely with Audi
in many of its race efforts.

Providing the power was a turbocharged 3.7-liter V6
diesel engine that produced 540ps!

In the Le Mans race in 2011, it famously battled with
Peugeot, where it proved victorious.

The Toyota Aqua was a smaller version of the popular Prius,
equipped with the same hybrid technology.

Not only was it super fuel efficient, Toyota made the car
fun to drive!

Note that the battery is located under the rear seats.

This allows for a lower center of gravity, which in turn,
results in better handling balance.w

No company has made a bigger splash in the electric
vehicle market than Tesla.

And, the Model S is its jewel in the crown.

Thanks to its low center of gravity, the car possesses
incredible handling balance.

This, and a very well-tuned suspension system, allow the
Model S to take corners like a true sports car.

The GT-R NISMO GT3 was designed for GT3-class racing
by Nissan's motorsports arm, NISMO.

The car you see here was prepared by a privateer, who
entered it in the Nürburgring 24 Hours in 2013.

And, here's an interesting tidbit, it was driven by
Kazunori Yamauchi, producer of Gran Turismo!

Which is why it comes loaded with simulation data from
Gran Turismo.

You might say it's more than just a car. We consider it
an integral part of Gran Turismo history!

The R.S. Trophy, based on the third-generation Mégane,
packs a good deal of performance.

It comes powered by a specially tuned 2-liter inline-4...

...that generates gobs of torque in the mid-RPM range, with
plenty of punch that made it a delight on the race track.

The R.S.'s forte is its handling, thanks to a suspension
designed for maximum front-tire grip.

This setup allow the car to enter corners with high speed
without having it understeer heavily.

In short, this thing is an absolute beast through corners.

Sure it’s small, but there is absolutely no doubt that
the Mercedes-Benz AMG A45 is the real deal!

It came with a 2.0-liter inline-4 under its hood that delivered
a surprisingly potent punch.

Combine that with its 4WD drivetrain, which provides excellent
stability, this thing is a blast to drive on a race track.

The third-generation Dodge Viper was definitely
in a class of its own.

The secret to its enhanced performance was a stronger
chassis with 50 percent more torsional rigidity.

This made it more stable through corners, so it handled better
than its predecessor, which is quite scary if you ask me.e

The C7 represented the seventh-generation Corvette.

This machine was no doubt the quintessential front-engine/
rear-wheel-drive (FR) sports car.

It came equipped with the LT1 engine, a 6.2-liter V-8...

...which pumped out a massive 461ps and 63kgm of torque.

Its new aluminum frame boasted improved rigidity, which
gave the car a stable and balanced handling feel.

The car was introduced on the Corvette's 60th anniversary...

and it was also the first model since the C2 to be given
the legendary Stingray moniker!

This fifth-generation Polo GTI, a petite hot hatch
one size smaller than the Golf...

was always considered the Golf's "little brother,"
ever since it was introduced in 1975.

This Polo GTI came with two different engines,
depending on the model.

Shown here is the late model that was introduced in 2014.
It came with a turbocharged 1.8-liter inline-4 engine...

...that produced 192ps and 25.5kgm of torque
from just 1250rpm!!

Small but speedy, this model also featured an upgraded
chassis and improved handling!

For many car enthusiasts, the 2005 Veyron was their first
exposure to the Bugatti brand.

It represented the first production car from the company
since it was revived in 1998.

The elegant proportions of its body are complemented by
the car's mid-mounted monster engine.

The W-16 produced more than 1000ps, allowing the car to
reach speeds of more than 400km/h!

Only 400 of these cars were made with production coming
to an end in 2015.

The 2013 Mercedes-Benz AMG VGT was the first car created for
the Vision Gran Turismo project.

Its design was inspired by the legendary Mercedes-Benz
300 SL, which was released in 1952.

The car's designers also drew inspiration from the dynamic
movement of big cats on the prowl.

It featured a lightweight carbon-fiber body, aluminum
space frame and a twin-turbocharged 5.5-liter V-8...

...which produced 585ps, enough to outrun a GT3 race car!

The spirit of the GTI was glorified with the GTI Roadster
Vision Gran Turismo!

This sporty, open-top 2-seater is a stunner!

You'll notice that its body makes use of various design
motifs from previous GTI models.

But perhaps the most striking aspect of its design
is the incredibly low-cut windscreen.

Appearances aside, it comes powered by a potent 510ps
twin-turbo 3.0-liter V-6.

Power is transferred to all four wheels, making this thing
an amazing handling machine.

The Genesis Coupe 3.8 Track is an FR sports car,
equipped with a 350ps 3.8-liter V-6.

Sharing its basic platform with the Genesis, Hyundai's
luxury sedan...

...the Track model of the Coupe 3.8 has been tuned for
increased performance.

Its specially designed suspension system and upgraded brakes
make it a beast on twisty roads.

This go-kart-like vehicle is a Gran Turismo original.

Equipped with a sequential 6-speed manual transmission
and a capable engine...

...it behaves much like a formula race car.

In fact, it can reach speeds of up to 200km/h,
depending on the gear ratio.

Don't let its appearance fool you. This is one mean puppy.

This hypothetical fan car was developed by Gran Turismo
in partnership with Red Bull Racing.

Despite its "Standard" name, it's anything but. In fact, this
machine is the higher-performing sibling of the X2014 Junior.

Under the hood is a turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-4
that produces a mean 810ps.

Employing a Venturi tunnel, the Standard can generate
gobs of downforce at high speed.

It does so by adapting the air pressure on the car
when it changes speed.

You might learn a thing or two about aerodynamics
by just driving this thing.

This hypothetical fan car was developed by Gran Turismo
in partnership with Red Bull Racing.

This baby is the entry-level model, not to be confused
with the higher-performing X2014 Standard.

Its aerodynamic body makes it a great choice for anyone
looking to learn how to drive a formula car.

Under the hood is a 250ps 2.0-liter inline-4 engine.

While Pagani is a relative newcomer to the
exclusive supercar world...

...its creations have certainly made a splash in the
short time they've been around.

The Huayra, successor to the Zonda, is one such car.

Featuring a carbon-fiber and titanium monocoque frame...

...it had a Mercedes-Benz AMG twin-turbo 6.0-liter V-12...

...which pumped out 700ps and 102kgm of torque.
That's definite super-car territory.

Indeed, company founder, Horacio Pagani, is quite proud
of his magnificent work of rolling art!<

The Toyota FT-1 was a concept car that was unveiled at
the 2014 North American International Auto Show.

Its design was used as the inspiration for the
production model of the GR Supra.

Toyota's North American design studio, Calty, led the
design process of this flashy sports car.

Look closely and you may notice that it was partly inspired
by previous Toyota FR sports cars!

sourceName: Aston Martin DP-100 Vision Gran Turismo
en:
The Aston Martin DP-100 Vision Gran Turismo is a product of
the Aston Martin design team led by Marek Reichman.

The mesmerizing blend of the brand’s past and future is
indeed a "Design Prototype," as the name "DP" suggests.

It comes powered by a mid-mounted twin-turbocharged V-12
that produces 811ps.

The fact that it remains one of the few mid-engine cars
Aston Martin ever produced only adds to its appeal!

In 2013, the BMW 4 Series was created to serve as the coupe
version of the company's popular 3 Series sedan.

Therefore, the M4 represented the top-of-the-line performance
version, taking the place of the M3 coupe.

Released in 2014, the M4 had rear-wheel drive...

...and came powered by a turbocharged 3.0-liter inline-6.

This powerful front-mounted engine cranked out 431ps
and 56.1kgm of torque!

The RX-8 is the last rotary-engine sports car from Mazda.

Its 4-door, 4-seat layout is unusual for a sports car.

This particular model is called the Spirit R,
the last of the RX-8s.

It's equipped with a 235ps naturally-aspirated engine
that's mated to a 6-speed manual transmission.

It's well-balanced with space for four people.8

sourceName: Mercedes-Benz AMG Vision Gran Turismo Racing Series
en:
The track version of the Mercedes-Benz AMG
Vision Gran Turismo is one monster of a car.

The base model's tuned engine is equipped with
a powerful racing transmission!

Weighing 85kg less than its predecessor, it goes and handles
better than you could ever imagine.

Inspired by the BMWs that made waves in the touring car
championships of the 1970s...

...this BMW Vision Gran Turismo is sure to remind you
of those classic race cars of yesteryear.

BMW's own design team was responsible
for bringing this creation to life.

Under the hood is a powerful turbocharged 3.0-liter
inline-6 engine.

And, as you might expect, this FR model has a
perfect 50/50 front/rear weight distribution.

Believe it or not, this road racer weighs a mere
1180kg!

Radical, a small English sports car manufacturer...

...specializes in making street-legal race cars,
such as the SR3 SL.

Powered by the Ford Focus' turbocharged
2.0-liter inline-4 that produces 240ps.

It's extremely lightweight at 775kg, and it possesses
a simple chassis devoid of electronic components.

True driving enthusiasts will love taking this for a ride.

sourceName: Concept XR-PHEV EVOLUTION Vision Gran Turismo
en:
This model served as the inspiration for
the Mitsubishi Concept XR-PHEV....

...which was unveiled at the Tokyo Motor Show
in 2013.

Known as the Concept XR-PHEV EVOLUTION VGT, it is powered
by an innovative plug-in hybrid system.

It also had an 8-speed dual-clutch transmission that
managed the impressive power of the drivetrain.

What’s more, it handled exceptionally well, thanks to
Mitsubishi's S-AWC 4-wheel-drive technology.

This car was inspired by the seventh-generation
Volkswagen Golf, often referred to as the Golf VII.

Powered by a turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-4 that delivers
up to 220ps of power and 35.7kgm of torque.

Its rigid chassis allows for stable and razor sharp
handling through even the trickiest of corners.

You're sure to have a thrilling and satisfying ride!d

After the Jaguar E-Type came the Jaguar F-Type, a sporty
rear-wheel-drive sports car for the modern age.

This particular model is the high-performance version
released in 2012.

It comes equipped with a supercharged 5.0-liter V-8
that produces 50ps more than the base model...

...bringing the grand total to an impressive 550ps!

Are you familiar with the Ford Mustang Mach 1 and GT40?

As the name suggests, the Mach 40 pays tribute to both of
these classic American race cars.

Produced by Eckert's Rod and Custom based in Oregon...

...this company specializes in custom restorations,
even creating original models from other cars.

This car has a fully customized body style of a
1969 Ford Mustang.

And it comes powered by the Ford GT's 5.4-liter V-8 engine,
mounted amidships.

This mesmerizing blend of two classics took home
the 2012 SEMA Gran Turismo Award!q

The TS030 Hybrid was Toyota's first ever hybrid race car,
designed for endurance events.

Developed to compete in the 2012 24 Hours of Le Mans
and World Endurance Championship...

...Toyota spent years refining its THS-R hybrid system.

The final product was realized through a collaboration between
Higashi-Fuji Technical Center and Toyota Motorsport.

Although its debut at Le Mans fell short of
the company's expectations...

It went on to claim an impressive 2nd place in the WEC!

The coachbuilding company Zagato is a legendary name
in the sports car world.

It should come as no surprise that Gran Turismo
decided to collaborate with the famed Italian company.

The design of this car was inspired by the Iso Rivolta,
an iconic tourer from the 1960s.

It was created as a vehicle that could compete
in the world's top racing events.

Underneath its very Zagato-esque body was a Callaway
4.5-liter V-8.

This powerplant pumped out a crazy 567ps!

sourceName: SUBARU VIZIV GT Vision Gran Turismo
en:
The VIZIV GT Vision Gran Turismo was all about Subaru's
pursuit of delivering a great driving experience.

Armed with a powerful hybrid power unit...

...this machine is powered by turbocharged 2.0-liter
flat-4 engine and three powerful electrical motors.

The power is distributed to all four wheels via Subaru's
all-wheel-drive system.

And the car's appearance is striking, is it not?

By the way, a fun fact about this design...

...it was inspired by the world's hardest food: "katsuobushi,"
a Japanese delicacy made of dried and fermented tuna!K
Buddy_ContentCar_BrandCentralOwner_normal_beat_91_1020171

The V12 Vantage was built to comply with FIA GT3 regulations
for 2012.

It came powered by a 5.9-liter V-12 engine, and weighed
1250kg lighter than its predecessor!

This car has seen plenty of success on the race track,
both in England and around the world.

The Toyota FT-1 Vision Gran Turismo is a car that redefines
the future of racing!

Its design is based on the FT-1, which was developed in the
pursuit of functional beauty.

You could say that this model takes that concept
to an entirely new level.

The large spoilers at the front and rear were installed after
closely studying their aerodynamic effect on the car.

It's clear no compromises were made on its styling,
either!

The 4C was Alfa Romeo's first mass-produced mid-engine
sports car.

A carbon-fiber monocoque helps reduce the car's curb
weight, leaving it at a mere 900kg.

You'll find the rigidity of its body improves the
precision of its handling.

Its design references the Alfa Romeo Tipo 33/2 Stradale,
once called "the most beautiful car in the world."

Many of Alpine's creations were successful race cars,
most notably in the WRC or at Le Mans.

The design of the Alpine Vision Gran Turismo was inspired
by some of those cars, including the A210 and A442B.

As you can see, it features an unusual single-seater design...

...which makes it lightweight and incredibly agile!

It also has side air brakes and other cool features
that are meant to enhance your driving experience.u

Chaparral was a maverick company that shook the racing world
in the 1960s

Time and again, they pulled off unique feats of
engineering, producing some truly unique race cars.

The Chevrolet Chaparral 2X Vision Gran Turismo is a tribute
to the Chaparral of decades past.

It doesn't just have an unusual body style...in fact,
everything about it defies convention!

For starters, it's powered by an innovative laser-based
propulsion system.

Its unusual configuration, which places the driver face-down,
was inspired by the riding position of a MotoGP racer.

The spirit of Jim Hall, who founded Chaparral,
is truly represented in this masterpiece!g

sourceName: SRT Tomahawk S Vision Gran Turismo
en:
Dodge's 3 Vision Gran Turismo cars represent the company's
vision for how racing will look in twenty years.

The SRT Tomahawk S VGT is the entry-level model.

Cutting-edge materials like carbon and graphene allow it
to weigh in at a mere 900kg.

And despite its "entry-level" designation, the engine
produces more than 1000ps!

I'd recommend mastering this model before moving on
to the two more high-performance cars!

sourceName: SRT Tomahawk GTS-R Vision Gran Turismo
en:
Dodge's 3 Vision Gran Turismo cars represent the company's
vision for how racing will look in twenty years.

The SRT The Tomahawk GTS-R VGT was designed
to take on the race track.

It comes powered by a V-10 engine that delivers
a whopping 1500ps!

And did I mention the car weighs a mere 663kg?

The car is so fast that it comes with a specially
designed G-suit to protect the driver!

sourceName: SRT Tomahawk X Vision Gran Turismo
en:
Dodge's 3 Vision Gran Turismo cars represent the company's
vision for how racing will look in twenty years.

And the SRT Tomahawk X VGT is the most advanced
of the three.

Its design was inspired by the concept of challenging
human boundaries.

That should explain why the engine was designed
to produce 2500ps!

The creators imagined that the car would reach speeds
that would push the limits of human reflexes.

Movable aerodynamic panels, like those found on a fighter
jet, are affixed to its body to provide maximum downforce.

All this and more allow you to take corners in this car at
speeds of 500km/h!;

Ferrari is known for making the sweetest-sounding V-12s ever.

In fact, the company's very first production car in 1947
came equipped with a V-12.

This F12berlinetta continued the trend with its 12-cylinder
powerplant mounted up front.

It boasted more than 700ps sending power to the rear wheels,
and its exterior design was stunning indeed.

The design was a collaboration between Ferrari's internal
design department and Pininfarina.

They're efforts led to the car winning the prestigious
Compasso d'Oro international design award in 2014.c

The LaFerrari was Ferrari's first car since the Enzo to
come equipped with a V-12 engine.

It was also the first ever production hybrid car
from the company.

The HY-KERS hybrid system in the LaFerrari was adapted from
Ferrari's Formula 1 machines.

It consisted of a 6.3-liter V-12 engine combined with two
electric motors providing a total output of 963ps.

This is the GT3 version of the Ferrari 458 Italia.

The base car's front and rear wings have been widened,
and the size of its aerodynamic parts increased.

The engine is largely the same as the base 458 Italia,
although some adjustments were made.

This particular model ran its first race in 2011.

And what a debut it was—it immediately proved a winner
in the FIA GT3 European Championship that year!

The Ford F-Series has consistently been one of the most
popular vehicles in the U.S.

This model, the SVT Raptor, was added to the lineup
in 2010.

It was developed for off-road use, with specially designed
dampers and an engine that produced more than 400ps.

Its interior looked like it came from a sports car.

Oh, and the "SVT" in its name stands for
"Special Vehicle Team,"....

…which is the division within Ford that's responsible for
developing the company's high-performance vehicles.

This concept car was the result of a collaboration between
Infiniti's design team and Gran Turismo.

While it has a very unique look, it clearly exhibits key
elements of Infiniti's design language.

Powered by an impressive 4.5-liter V-8 combined with
an electric motor...

...its hybrid system was based on those found
in Formula 1 race cars.

A front mid-engine transaxle gives it a sporty 45:55 front/rear
weight distribution, making it virtually race ready.H

If I had to describe the Mini Clubman Vision Gran Turismo
in simple terms, it would be "battle-ready."

The car sits much wider and lower to the ground than the
classic model, looking ready to attack the race track.

Indeed, that's what it was created to do. Maximum performance
is ensured with lots of aerodynamic features.

And it's lightweight. It tips the scales at 1050kg and comes
powered by an impressive engine that produces 400ps.

Also, its full-time 4WD drivetrain provides plenty
of stability.

The Mazda LM55 Vision Gran Turismo is a real beauty!

It's the perfect iteration of Mazda's "KODO: Soul of Motion"
design philosophy.

One of the inspirations for its styling was the legendary
787B race car that made history at Le Mans.

The designers attempted to capture the past and future of Mazda
in a single design, and I'd say they succeeded.

Its powertrain is capable of incredible power, efficiency,
and durability.

And who knows? Perhaps a victory at Le Mans is on the cards
for this mean machine too.

The GTI Supersport Vision Gran Turismo offers a hint of what
the future may hold for the Golf GTI.

This hatchback-styled vehicle is, in fact, a powerful
2-seater sports car.

The classic Golf's chassis has been upgraded for racing,
with a lower center of gravity and much lighter weight.

It's also equipped with 4-wheel drive and an engine
that churns out more than 500ps.

Not bad for a Golf, right?

After its class win at the 2008 24 Hours of
Le Mans...

...there was little doubt that the DBR9 GT1 was destined
to be a British race car classic.

It came powered by a 5.9-liter V-12 that left most of its
competition in the dust.

It turned in impressive performances in numerous other events,
that is, until the GT1 category was discontinued in 2011.

Take the beauty of the LF-LC, a concept car by Lexus, combine
it with the striking silhouette of a race car...

...and you get the Lexus LF-LC GT VGT!

This gorgeous vehicle was designed to race in touring-car
such as the Super GT or Nürburgring 24 Hours.

It's race-ready for the virtual race track.

The Mercedes-AMG GT is Mercedes-Benz's flagship sports car.

This 2-seat FR machine combines the elegance of the company's
luxury image with the sportiness of its racing heritage.

This high-performance GT S version came equipped with an
engine that produced 50ps more than the base model.

The Peugeot Vision Gran Turismo is all about performance.

This remarkable car was developed by Peugeot's design team
and the engineers responsible for the Peugeot Sport.

Its turbocharged 3.2-liter V-6 engine, mounted amidships,
pumped out a hearty 887ps.

Particular attention was paid to endurance race cars during
the development of this efficiently-designed model.

You can see this in its aerodynamic parts, which are kept
to an absolute minimum without affecting performance.

Everything about the Honda Sports Vision Gran Turismo
was designed with the driver in mind.

The compact mid-engine machine epitomizes Honda's take
on the ideal sports car.

The design team put this model through real-life tests when
developing its aerodynamics.

Under the hood is a 410ps turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-4.

Shifting is performed via an 8-speed dual-clutch gearbox.

It's a real rocket — the car weighs only 899kg!S

The Lexus RC F is a pretty exciting GT3 race machine.

Did you know that the "F" in its name stands for the Fuji
Speedway, the home course for Lexus Gazoo Racing?

The naturally-aspirated 5.0-liter V-8 engine isn't just
powerful, it revs smoothly to the red line.

The enhanced oil cooler allows drivers to get the most
out of their time on the race track.

Although it's considered an eco-friendly car, the Fit Hybrid
is actually quite sporty.

This third-generation model came with a 1.5-liter engine and
a 7-speed DCT.

Although it wasn't particularly fast, it wasn't slow either.

The chassis had a lower center of gravity, enabling the car
to possess stable handling characteristics.

sourceName: Alpine Vision Gran Turismo Race Mode
en:
This race version of the Alpine Vision Gran Turismo
looks pretty impressive, doesn't it?

The configuration of the canards and headlights
embody the race car aesthetic.

Yes, this recent installment in the long line of Alpine
race cars is a worthy successor to that classic tradition.

This machine was introduced to celebrate Lamborghini's 50th
anniversary.

Called the Veneno, it was unveiled at the 2013
Geneva Motor Show.

This coupe model was a one-off, made especially for
display at the show.

However, the company built three more to meet the
demands of passionate Lamborghini aficionados.

Later, nine roadsters were produced for sale.

Each Veneno is a one-of-a-kind example that has a solid place
in Lamborghini history.

How much does it cost? Well, if you have to ask,
you probably can't afford it.

The Hyundai N 2025 Vision Gran Turismo was created to celebrate
the South Korean manufacturer's 50th anniversary.

The "N" in its name is reserved for cars that possess
the highest performance in the company's lineup.

It is the power unit in particular that sets this car apart.

This model is powered by hub motors, utilizing fuel-cell
technology developed by Hyundai.

Weighing in at just north of one ton, the N 25 Gran Turismo
is lightweight and quite nice to look at.[

The Dodge Charger SRT is among the world's most
powerful sedans.

With more than 700ps on tap, it can reach speeds
of approximately 330km/h.

In case you didn't know, the "SRT" in its name stands for
Street and Racing Technology.

It's made up of a group of engineers within Dodge who specialize
in developing high-performance vehicles.

This means that if you see a car with an SRT badge on it, you
might want to think twice before challenging it to a race.

If you're in the market for a fun rear-wheel-drive sports car,
you can't go wrong with this Mazda MX-5.

This fourth-generation model is known as the ND.

More than 100kg lighter than its predecessor, it embraced
all the virtues that made the original so popular.

The S-segment ND is good looking, lightweight and
an absolute joy to drive.

Like its predecessors, the third-generation BMW M3 represented
the ultimate in the FR performance-sedan genre.

Its naturally-aspirated inline-6 engine was virtually
race ready, boasting more than 100ps per liter.

This truly exceptional piece of machinery was hailed as
the most powerful inline-6 in the world.

With a stylish body and exceptional handling balance, this
car is truly one of the treasures in BMW's rich vault.s

The WRX STI is the pinnacle of the highly popular
Impreza WRX line.

Introduced in 2014, it is equipped with a turbocharged
variant of Subaru's legendary EJ20 boxer engine.

It's mated to an improved 6-speed manual gearbox
with short throws.

Like previous models, this one features all-wheel drive.

The WRX STI was designed to go fast on a variety
of different driving surfaces.[

The sixth-generation Mustang represented a big step
in the model's evolutionary process.

For the first time, it utilized a 4-wheel independent
suspension system.

This dramatically improved the handling of the car, allowing
it to corner like a true well-balanced sports car.

Base models were equipped with a peppy turbocharged
inline-4 engine.

However, the GT had Ford's legendary V-8, which produced
441ps and 40kgm of torque.x

The Nissan GT-R LM Nismo made its debut at
the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015.

It competed in the Le Mans Prototype 1 Hybrid class.

To the surprise of many, it utilized a
front-engine/front-wheel-drive layout.

It was an unusual design for an LMP1 vehicle, some
problems had to be resolved before it was ready.

While the car didn't perform particularly well in the race,
it did leave a lasting impression on all who saw it.s

sourceName: DAIHATSU COPEN RJ Vision Gran Turismo
en:
The Daihatsu Copen RJ Vision Gran Turismo was built to
comply with Japan's "kei car" specifications.

The engine is set at 660cc, it can produce 150ps,
almost 2.5 times as much as the standard Copen.

The "RJ" in the name stands for Racing Jacket.

You really feel like you are wearing the car
when sitting in the driver's seat.

Bugatti has always been a company that drew inspiration
from its racing history.

The case is no different with this model that embodied
the very soul of the marque.

It was partly based on the company's classic race car,
the Type 57 Tank....

...which took the overall title at the 24 Hours of Le Mans
race twice in the 1930s.

The mid-mounted W-16 engine was tuned to produce up to 1673ps.%

This ultra-lightweight pure sports car concept was born from
the collaboration between Honda and Gran Turismo.

The design theme drew inspiration from Honda's first
Formula 1 race cars in the 1960s.

Its power unit incorporates technologies developed
for superbikes.

The engine is normally used in the Honda RC213V-S,
which is a MotoGP class motorcycle.

The car demonstrates the company's ability to compete in
all manner of races, be it on two wheels or four.H

Chris Holstrom Concepts is a hot rod shop in the Pacific
Northwest that specializes in custom designs.

This car was built using a Chevy Nova as a base...

...and powered by a supercharged V-8 that belonged in
the Corvette ZR1.

This powerplant produced up to 700ps.

This car won the Gran Turismo Award at the SEMA show, the
largest showcase of custom automobiles in the world.

The S-FR was a concept vehicle unveiled at the 2015
Tokyo Motor Show.

While this lightweight RWD sports car was designed for everyday
use, it certainly turned heads at the show.

With a compact body on par with the AE86, its weight is
evenly distributed over the front and rear axles.

The design was inspired by the famous Toyota Sports 800.

The Toyota 86 GRMN is the gentleman racer's 86.

It employs lightweight pistons, a custom crankshaft...

...and an upgraded exhaust system.

Also, it sports a carbon-fiber roof and hood, with upgraded
brakes reinforced with special materials.

Oh, and the "MN" in its name stands for "Meister of Nürburgring."

This means that the car was the result of the company's
participation in the Nürburgring 24 Hour race.

It's the ideal sports car, one that's fast and easy to drive.x

The Demio is Mazda's entry-level model.

This fourth-generation version was introduced in 2014.

Power is supplied by a turbocharged 1.5-liter diesel engine
that produces 25kgm of torque.

Because of its predictable handling character, this car is
ideal for novices learning how to race.<

The Huracán is one of a long line of Lamborghini V-10 models.

It served as the base model for the company's GT3 race cars.

This LP610-4 has a mid-engine 4-wheel-drive layout.

It's handling is on another level, thanks to the grip and
traction provided by 4WD and the sport-tuned suspension system.

Its ten-cylinder engine can produces more than 600ps
and delivers it with a sweet, melodic roar.

This version of the Ferrari 458 Italia is a Gran Turismo
Gr.4 original.

It has fewer aerodynamic modifications, but retains the
tremendous downforce generated by the original 458.

This third-generation Vantage served as the base for this
Gran Turismo-exclusive Gr.4 race car.

And, as you would expect from a front-engine/rear-wheel-drive
premium sports car, its handling character was divine.

Under the hood was a sweet-sounding V-8 that was as responsive
as it was powerful, making it a delight to drive on the track.8

Not too many compact sports cars are as well-balanced as the
third-generation TT, which was designated TTS.

In addition to being 50kg lighter than its base model...

...it came equipped with Audi's signature quattro AWD system
that gave the TTS unrivaled agility, especially in the wet.

For novices learning their way around a track,
this thing was ideal.

The Genesis Coupe served as the foundation for this
Gran Turismo Gr.4 race car.

Its long wheelbase and traditional FR layout made it an
ideal candidate to transform it into a race car.

Extensive tuning and significant weight reduction give this car
the feel of a GT3 machine.

The Genesis Coupe served as the foundation for this
Gran Turismo-exclusive Gr.3 race car.

And what a well-balanced machine it is, because the car already
possessed many race car attributes.

The most notable thing about the original was its handling,
which was both stable and predictable.

Its long wheelbase allowed for a spacious interior, while its
profile provided excellent downforce at high speed.

The sixth-generation Mustang served as the foundation for
this original Gran Turismo-exclusive Gr.4 race car.

Throughout its history, the legendary pony car from Ford
has been converted to compete on the race track.

There's a reason for this: The Mustang is simply one of the
most well-balanced sports cars America has ever produced.

The sixth-generation Mustang served as the foundation
for this Gran Turismo-exclusive Gr.3 race car.

One of the Mustang's great attributes was its speed.

That said, its improved handling made it a well-rounded
race car.x

This original Gran Turismo Gr.4 race car used the
Alfa Romeo 4C as its foundation.

The lightweight construction and impressive mobility of
the 4C made it a great candidate for our Gr.4 races.B

The third-generation Renault Sport Mégane served as the base
for this Gran Turismo-exclusive Gr.4 race car.

With traction second to none, this car takes sharp
corners with ease.

The Mégane's celebrated handling remains a key feature of
this racing variant.

This Gr.4 Gran Turismo-exclusive race car used the Nissan GT-R
for its foundation.

The inclusion of fog lights on the car's front bumper
really give it the endurance race car looks.

On the track, the car's powerful engine and remarkable
AWD handling provide a potent combination.W

To specially designate its lineup of plug-in hybrids and EVs...

...BMW used the letter "i" in the vehicle name,
such as in the compact i3.

The i3 was the company's first mass-produced electric car.

With 170ps of power and 25kgm of torque, the i3's drivetrain
provided excellent acceleration.

BMW worked hard to keep the car's weight down, using carbon-fiber
reinforced polymer to keep it at a lean 1260kg.

The name Renault Sport may not be familiar here in the States,
but in Europe, it's one of the most well-known sporty brands.

It's the name of the motorsports division of the company, which
has participated in everything from Formula 1 to Le Mans.

The fourth-generation Clio is a great example of
the types of cars it produces.

Providing the power for this compact is a turbocharged
1.6-liter inline-4 that produced 220ps.

The "Trophy" version was created as a special model
specifically for race-track use.

To see how fast the car was, the folks at Renault Sport
took it to the Nürburgring.

And guess what? The thing ended up setting a new lap record
for compact hatchbacks!

The DS3 received its name from a line of luxury cars from Citroën
that were marketed from 1955 to 1975.

But the DS3, produced in 2009 to 2016, had very little
in common with those original models.

This car placed performance first, eventually becoming
one of the Continent's most popular hot hatches.

The DS3 Racing version was used as the foundation for the
French company's entry in the World Rally Championship.

A number of engine options were available, but the turbocharged
1.6-liter inline-4 was the most powerful at 200ps.

Development of the car was overseen by Citroën Racing.&

The third-gen Atenza's handling reflects Mazda’s
"Jinba Ittai": the unity between car and driver.

Equipped with a turbocharged 2.2-liter diesel
inline-4, mated to a 6-speed manual gearbox.

And then, there's Mazda’s Skyactive Technology.

The company's signature engineering principles,
embedded throughout the vehicle.

Combined with the attractive styling inside and out,
you have one very intriguing and capable sports sedan.

This Gran Turismo Gr.4 original race car is based on
the BMW M4.

At first glance, it might looks like an M Performance Edition,
but it has a few mods, like the spoilers and hood pin.

Its design is reminiscent of the safety cars used in today's
popular race series.

The third-generation Focus ST's engine pumps out 250ps,
which is 25ps more than its predecessor.

This later version was produced after a minor change
to the model in 2015.

The suspension setting was revised, which improved
handling, most notably sharper turn-in response.

It also received a slight facelift, giving the car a leaner,
sportier overall appearance. q

The Peugeot VGT was the base model for this Gran
Turismo Gr.3 original race car.

To meet Gr.3 specs, the engine and chassis were
heavily modified.

On the outside, you'll notice that a rear wing and front
splitter were added to improve the car's aerodynamics.

The base model for this Gran Turismo-exclusive Gr.4 race car
was none other than the Toyota 86.

With 346ps on tap and remarkable handling, this machine
had the power and grace of a GT3 racer.w

This Vision Gran Turismo Gr.3 was based on the
GTI Roadster.

The front splitter and rear wing were designed to work
together to dramatically increase downforce.

This version is a rear-wheel driver, changed from
the base car's 4WD system.

Serving as the foundation for the Gran Turismo Gr.3 race car
was the Peugeot RCZ.

While the original came with an FF layout, we changed it to an
MR layout to suit Gr.3 specifications.

This was easily done, thanks to the base RCZ's long wheelbase,
which provides exceptional lateral stability.

We must say that the car's overall balance has been greatly
improved with the new engine location. %

The prized qualities of Mitsubishi's famed AWD sports sedan
are on display in the Lancer Evolution's Final Edition.

At the heart of every Evo is the engine.

The one in this car produces 313ps and 43.7kgm of torque,
making it the most powerful Evo engine ever.

Not only are the suspension and brakes also impressive...

...the technically-advanced AWD system makes this a monster
on all types of terrain.

The Nissan Concept 2020 VGT was the culmination of
Nissan's storied involvement with motorsports.

Nissan Design Europe, based in London, England,
did most of the design work here...

...while all the technical stuff was undertaken by the
company's engineers based in Japan.

What made this car unique was its "performance hybrid FR-4WD"
layout that consisted of a twin-turbocharged V-6...

...combined with three electric motors, where the front
left and right motors worked independently.

Therefore, this car was, as its name suggested, an AWD vehicle.

With torque being distributed independently to each wheel, the
Nissan Concept 2020 VGT possessed remarkable handling.

The Audi R8 LMS was developed in accordance with
FIA GT3 regulations.

This second-generation model made its debut in 2015.

Shortly after its release, it ran in the Nürburgring
24 Hours, where it surprisingly won the race.

The downforce generated by its body, which provided stability
at high speed, was arguably its greatest strength.

really fast on an off-road trail. 8

This Gran Turismo-exclusive Gr.B rally car is based on
the Subaru WRX STI.

The body is specifically designed to provide maximum
downforce at high speeds.

And, the wider tires and suspension are specifically
developed for driving on the dirt.

This Gran Turismo-exclusive Gr.B rally car is based on the
Peugeot RCZ.

There's a popular event in Colorado called the Pikes Peak
International Hill Climb.

And, as you can see from the huge front and rear wings,
this car was designed specifically to win that race.

The engine is mounted amidships, providing power to
all four wheels.

This Gran Turismo-exclusive Gr.B rally car is based on the
sixth-generation Ford Mustang.

The livery is inspired by the Ford GT race car.

The four lights mounted on the hood and wide body give
the car a menacing presence.

Underneath the body, the suspension has been strengthened
to keep ride quality stable.

The original car was rear-wheel drive, but this one has been
converted to 4WD.

This Gran Turismo-exclusive Gr.B rally car is based on the
Ford Focus ST.

The drivetrain has been converted from powering only the
front wheels to 4WD.

Various changes have also been made to alter the weight
distribution, such as moving the radiator to the rear.

The handling is considerably sharper as a result.Q

This Gran Turismo-exclusive safety car is based on the
Mercedes AMG GT S.

It comes equipped with essential safety-car equipment, such
as a revolving light on the roof and flashing headlights.

The AMG GT S is known for having been the official safety
car of Formula 1 from 2015 to 2017.

This Gran Turismo-exclusive Gr.1 race car is based on the
McLaren Ultimate Vision Gran Turismo-exclusive.

Power is restricted to 950ps as per regulations,
but it packs a serious punch nonetheless.

McLaren's driver-focused technology makes this a formidable
weapon on any race track.

Peugeot Sport's 208 GTi picked up the hot hatch mantle
from the legendary 205 GTi.

The car employed an FF layout, meaning its engine was
mounted in front and powered the front wheels.

With a more compact body than its predecessor, the 207,
it weighed more than a 100kg less.

The engine came in the form of a turbocharged 1.6-liter inline-4
that produced 200ps and 28kgm of torque.

The 60.8km Isle of Man TT is renowned for being
one of the most dangerous races in the world.

At first only motorcycles ran the course, but for the
past few years, cars were added to the list.

Subaru has been a familiar sight at the Isle of Man event,
challenging it since 2011 with cars like this one.

This WRX's turbocharged 2.0-liter flat-4 has been tuned
to produce an amazing 600ps.

The engine and other performance parts were tuned by STI,
which stands for Subaru Tecnica International.

The motorsports arm of Subaru was also responsible
for the company's dominance in WRC.O

This Lexus RC F GT3 was created to wage war in the FIA GT3
championships.

This car has seen action in Japanese Super GT races, the U.S.
IMSA Series, and the European GT Series.

And the amazing thing is that this svelte Lexus machine
has won in every series it has appeared in!

This Gran Turismo-exclusive Gr.B rally car is an original
based on the Honda NSX.

It has unique custom suspension, ensuring plenty of ground
clearance and an ability to handle the harshest terrain.

Because of its mid-engine/AWD layout, the car's weight
distribution is biased towards the rear.

This Gran Turismo-exclusive Gr.B rally car is based on
the Hyundai Genesis Coupe.

It has been adapted to take on any dirt road, as its
rear-wheel-drive layout was converted to AWD.

The tires are also wider, now measuring a whopping 2050mm.

Despite a relatively long wheelbase, it makes no
compromises in maneuverability.

The organic undulations of its front bumper and rally-
ready aerodynamics make it look as good as it goes.

This Gran Turismo-exclusive Gr.B rally monster
is based on the Nissan GT-R.

It comes equipped with a rally suspension system,
tuned specifically for driving on the dirt.

It also has an extra set of four fog lamps, making it
ready to race in the dead of night.

This Gran Turismo-exclusive Gr.B rally car is based on
the sporty Toyota 86.

Its two-layered rear spoiler and other aerodynamic elements
help make it a truly state-of-the-art rally machine.

The drivetrain has been adapted from rear-wheel drive to AWD,
ensuring appropriate grip and traction on the dirt.

It's no secret that many of Porsche's road-going masterpieces
were the product of the company's racing heritage.

The 911 GT3 RS is no different.

The engine and suspension were custom-built for this car.

And extra steps were taken to reduce the weight,
including the installation of a magnesium roof.

The 991 was the first GT3 RS car to add rear-wheel
steering to its formidable array of features.

If you want to go fast anywhere from the open road to a
challenging race track, this car should be high on your list.

This Vision Gran Turismo celebrates the Porsche brand
in the form of a lightweight sports car.

It features a state-of-the-art carbon-fiber monocoque and a
beautiful glass canopy.

The design pays tribute to classic Porsches from the past,
including the 356 roadster.

The power unit was inspired the 919 endurance race car
and the all-electric Taycan.

It features two motors, one in the front and the other at the
rear of the car.

This "dual electric engine" produces an impressive
1114ps through an AWD layout.

The car remains incredibly stable at high speed, too,
thanks to its active aero systems.k

The 996 GT3 was a true labor of love for Porsche's
top engineers.

In fact, this high-performance model reinvented the 911 genre.

First, instead of the traditional air-cooled engine, this one
came with a water-cooled boxer powerplant.

Thanks to its excellent power and race-ready chassis, the GT3
served as the foundation for many race cars.

Some say it's the true successor to the 993 Carrera RS.

But everyone agrees it's a car that will go down
in Porsche history.d

The Taycan is Porsche's first fully electric vehicle.

The motors are incredibly powerful and super
responsive as you would expect from a Porsche.

The steering system and brakes are also world-class.

The Turbo S, which is the top-of-the-line model,
delivers a massive 761ps.

This Gran Turismo-exclusive safety car is based on the
Nissan GT-R.

The LED lights on the roof and bumpers provide helpful
information for drivers on the track.

They are controlled by a set of specially-designed
switches inside the car9

This Gran Turismo-exclusive Gr.3 race car is based on
the Volkswagen Beetle.

It has undergone a number of special improvements, including
being converted from a front-drive car to a rear-wheel drive.

With its wide fenders and missing roof, there's not
much of the original car left in this machine.

This road car was designed as a homologated
Alfa Romeo 4C Gr.3.

It features a 450ps engine mounted on a chassis with a long
wheelbase designed for the 4C Gr.3.x

This road car was designed as a homologated
Corvette C7 Gr.3.

At 2050mm, it's the maximum allowable width for a
Gr.3 racer.

Its chassis retains all the hallmarks of its race car
forebears, and the handling is very responsive.-

This road car was designed as a homologated
Ford Mustang Gr.3.

There is absolutely nothing standard about its acceleration
or cornering capabilities.

It's a powerful FR, making it a great choice for anyone
who wants to do some drifting.

sourceName: Lancer Evolution Final Edition    Gr.B Road Car
en:
This N-class road car was designed as a homologated
version of the Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution Gr.B.

The weight is evenly distributed between front and rear, and
its 4WD system provides plenty of grip through corners.

This one truly breaks the rallying mold, making for
a hugely enjoyable on-road experience.

This road car was designed as a homologated
Peugeot RCZ Gr.3.

The mid-engine layout allows for the glamorous proportions that
give it its unique look.

The design brings to mind Peugeot's 2002 "RC" concept.

And it may have been the original inspiration here.
The RC also had a mid-mounted engine, after all!A

This road car was designed as a homologated
Subaru WRX Gr.B.

The chassis is taken wholesale from the Gr.B rally version.

However, the aerodynamic parts show that on-road performance
was also a consideration.

In fact, the side panels and rear diffuser make road racing
seem like the focus here.

The Clubsport is a Porsche Cayman GT4 designed for
racing on the track.

In terms of power, it's no different from the base model.

However, changes to the shape, underbody and power train
mean it's much more competition-focused.

The change from a 6-speed manual to a two-pedal DCT
transmission also help maximize performance.B

The 991 version of the 911 RSR is a race car designed for
endurance events such as the 24 Hours of Le Mans.

The biggest departure from the stock 911 is
its mid-mounted engine.

Considerable aerodynamic improvements were also implemented,
making this machine stable at high speeds.

sourceName: Fittipaldi EF7 Vision Gran Turismo by Pininfarina
en:
Emerson Fittipaldi is one of the true legends of motorsports.
His credentials include...

...two-time Formula 1 champion...

...two-time Indy 500 winner...

...and now, car designer. This Vision Gran Turismo model is
his take on the perfect race car.

Its official name is the Fittipaldi EF7 VGT by Pininfarina.

The concept was to create a car that anyone could drive,
but one that could also be a serious racing contender.

And as anyone taking the wheel will see, that concept
has become reality.=

This race car, based on the third-generation Audi TT, was
designed to compete in a one-make race.

Called Audi Sport TT Cup, it began as a support series for
the German Touring Car Masters in 2015.

As for the car, it was a bit different from the road car,
thanks to a few improvements.

For example, while the engine was the same turbocharged inline-4
as the TTS, it came with more power, rated at 300ps.

It also featured a large adjustable rear wing.~

This road car was designed as a homologated
Mazda Atenza Gr.3.

Its key features are Gr.3-worthy handling and a powerful
400ps engine.

A true expression of Mazda's "KODO" design philosophy...

Every detail has been considered, right down to how its body
reflects light.t

This fourth-generation Clio was tuned by Renault Sport.

The R.S. 220 EDC Trophy boasted a strengthened
chassis and a custom 220ps engine.

Certain styling elements made it look a bit more intriguing
than the standard 2016 model.

It was a car that truly looked as good as it drove.

This 2017 Alpine Vision Gran Turismo is based on
its predecessor from 2014.

Not only was the engine power increased to
a massive 603ps...

...its drivetrain was converted to a rear-engine,
rear-wheel-drive layout.

If you take this thing near its top speed, you'll notice
that the car's aerodynamics were enhanced as well.B

The Audi e-tron Vision Gran Turismo is a fully electric
version of the original Audi VGT.

Its unique styling is the work of Audi Design, the company's
in-house design department.

The body graphics are inspired by those from the classic
Audi 90 IMSA GTO.

With one motor at the front axle and two at the rear,
it was AWD with a total power output of 815ps.

The Audi race team loved this design study so much, they even
went as far as to build one in real life!%

Held in Las Vegas, Nevada, the SEMA Show is the world's
largest automotive aftermarket event.

The car you see here, the Wicked Fabrication GT 51...

...won the "Best in Show Gran Turismo Award" at the
2016 SEMA Show.

It was designed by former racing driver Bruce Leven...

...and built at the Wicked Fabrication factory in Alabama.

To realize a modern-day classical racing Ford...

...Leven based his creation on a 1951 Ford Custom Club Coupe.

He installed a race-tuned V-8 under the hood and reinforced
the chassis for serious track sessions.

According to Wicked Fabrication, more than 10,000 hours
were spent in building this special car.

The AMG F1 W08 EQ Power+ dominated the
2017 Formula 1 season.

The engine was a turbocharged 1.6-liter V-6 with a
unique integrated hybrid energy recovery unit.

The car was driven by Lewis Hamilton and
Valtteri Bottas.

Between the two of them, they notched up an
impressive 12 victories in 20 races.

This performance earned Hamilton his fourth
World Drivers Championship.

Mercedes AMG also claimed its
fourth consecutive Constructors Championship.

There's nothing quite like a 1980s Formula 1 car.

They were stylish, powerful and downright raw, with
gobs of power and incredible sound.

Gran Turismo thought of bringing back the mystique
of that golden era with this car.

Powering this machine is a turbocharged 1.6-liter V-6
that recalls the classic engines of the day.

And it packs some serious Formula 1 heat, too.
How's 1000ps at 11000rpm?

If you want to feel a pure Formula 1 race car,
give this one a try.

This is what you get when you add racing-level
capabilities to the already formidable AMG GT.

Custom turbochargers raise the power to a 585ps.

And the suspension has been updated to incorporate
the technology used in today's GT3 race cars.

Thanks to the addition of a rear-wheel-steering system,
this car has razor-sharp handling character.

So, if you want to enjoy neck-wrenching cornering with amazing
straight-line performance, this is the car for you.

The GR Supra Racing Concept appeared on the motorsports scene
before the new GR Supra hit the production line.

This created quite the stir for Japanese-car enthusiasts
everywhere.

The development concept for this car was to create a contender
for the Le Mans LM-GTE class.

Mission accomplished because this Supra made for the ideal
endurance racer right out of the gate.B

If such a thing as the archetypal sports car happens to exist,
then this may be it.

Building on the concept of the Type 996, the 997 featured
improved engine capabilities among other things.

This late-model version was released in 2008.

Engine displacement was increased to 3.8 liters, which
increased power by 20ps to 435ps.
